original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.
Extending a source-count census without naming a supplier/interface decision it could change; audit #2973 pruning concerns before relying on the affected predecessor exclusions.

actual_scope: Exact unit-call optimum 2p^2+2p-4 for every odd prime p, two immutable sources, all nonzero F_p^2 coefficient rows, one dirty restored connector, and only signed source/readout complete calls.
scope_change_reason: Changes binary-mask demand to full prime-field coefficient demand and permits signed letters. This is a local exact side result, not a claim of a completed supplier budget.
bottleneck_link: Signed source/readout calls are a concrete priced alphabet change at the generic connector boundary. This theorem supplies an exact local bill; a recursive full-coefficient consumer and all physical costs remain unknown.
stop_rule: Stop research at the first verified original result. Package the square construction and all-word lower bound; do not pursue composite characteristics, additional sources or weighted optima.
evidence: Written uniform proof; exact constructions at p=3,5,7,11,13; complete short-source censuses of 85 and 21845 words at p=3,5; ten dense dirty noncommuting fixtures; ten rejection controls. A generated stdout receipt binds all five package files.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: What is the exact optimum with unequal complete call prices?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A physical caller may have source and readout prices that favor more readouts.
open_questions.first_step: At p=5 compare explicitly priced short source words against their missing-row readout costs.
open_questions.blocked_by: The unit-price lower bound does not solve weighted trades.

open_questions.question: What changes for composite characteristic or extension-field coefficients?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The prime-field result does not classify other coefficient alphabets.
open_questions.first_step: Specify the coefficient set and legal scalar letters before extending the lattice argument.
open_questions.blocked_by: No theorem outside odd prime fields is supplied.

open_questions.question: Which recursive caller needs every nonzero coefficient row in F_p^2?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Only a complete physical consumer can turn this call count into a supplier saving.
open_questions.first_step: Pin one caller and price admission, signed primitives, dispatch and dirty return.
open_questions.blocked_by: Caller, stock, precision and physical cost obligations are unknown.

result: OPT_signed(p,2)=2p^2+2p-4 for every odd prime p. In particular OPT_signed(5,2)=56, with eight source calls and 48 readouts.
